sources_considered.why: Primary GPT-3 experiments document sampled generation and systematic differences between models and a deliberately degraded control.
A contemporary training intervention changed instruction following and factual-error frequency.
Relevant additional research on patterned errors, but not needed for the narrower conclusion that chance alone is insufficient.

receipt.public_excerpt: a 160M parameter model with no context and increased output randomness.

evidence_items.explanation: Human detection accuracy was about 86% for the degraded control and 52% for GPT-3, with outputs selected programmatically. This supports systematic competence beyond random text, although the control changes several factors together.

receipt.public_excerpt: They also make up facts less often

evidence_items.explanation: The disclosure describes next-word training and subsequent training with human feedback, which improved instruction following and reduced fabricated facts. These systematic effects support learned mechanisms as an explanation beyond chance alone.
